neighbours.label: The name of a lamp's light-producing technology (xenon, halogen, LED backlight, CCFL), vs other component names in the same devices
fire: The car's headlights were upgraded from old bulbs to bright xenon units.
A small halogen spotlight lit the painting from above.
The film projector needs a new xenon bulb every few thousand hours.
The kitchen has halogen downlights fitted into the ceiling.
Older laptop screens used a CCFL tube to light the display.
The aquarium is lit by a strip of LED backlight under the hood.
Stadium floodlights often use metal halide or xenon arc lamps.
The reading lamp takes a twenty-watt halogen capsule.
quiet: The car's wipers were upgraded from old blades to quiet rubber ones.
A small brass hook held the painting from above.
The film projector needs a new drive belt every few thousand hours.
The kitchen has oak cupboards fitted along the back wall.
Older laptop screens used a thick plastic hinge to hold the display.
The aquarium is cleaned by a small pump under the hood.
Stadium seats often use moulded plastic or aluminium frames.
The reading lamp takes a ten-metre extension cable.

predictions: Light-source names 0.6-1.6 (peaking on split pieces like Xen|on, hal|ogen); other device parts 0.0-0.3.
notes: Card: Xen|on x3, ' illumination', 背|光, CC|FL, ' lamp', ' light', lam|пы. Probe: xenon lamp 1.634, halogen bulb 1.351, LED backlight 0.614, desk lamp 0.114; projector fan 0.302, focus knob 0.250, TV stand 0.010. The pole is strongest on the technology name, not on 'lamp'.
